prose_updates.tldr: One randomized panel of deterministic machine-learning policies must support sharp causal validation of a prespecified update library. The finite-\(\Gamma\) nearest-matching-score width is exact both for the aggregate cell-mean class and for a source-faithful individual-level Chen--Oberst subclass, because homogenization makes their induced mean surfaces coincide. Under the actual bounded no-Lipschitz Chen--Oberst class, the exact prospective cell cost is zero only for a selected matching neutral arm or a selected matching nonneutral arm at exactly the target score, and is one otherwise; homogeneous common endpoint schedules prove sharpness. The rational panel problem has an exact deterministic certificate generator and independent checker: generation always terminates, the three-cell, at-most-five-candidate audit agrees with exhaustive enumeration and the mixed-integer formulation, and a computable coordinatewise-minimizer condition yields a one-node polynomial certificate. Simultaneous assignment-only coverage remains the supporting inference result.

project_justification.gap: ChenOberst2025 supplies tight monotonicity-only reusable-validation bounds under unit-level performance monotonicity and neutral-action equality, but not the finite-\(\Gamma\) prospective nearest-score panel identity. AnthonyGoyalGuptaNagarajan2010 supplies the robust scenario nearest-facility skeleton, while generic exact-proof-log work motivates independently checkable optimization records but does not provide the specialized deterministic rational generator, bounded exact audit, or causal-tensor compression condition proved here.
project_justification.niche: The field niche is the causal derivation of the exact design loss: a faithful bridge shows that the finite-\(\Gamma\) common-schedule and width results remain exact on an individual-level Chen--Oberst subclass, while a separate theorem recovers the genuine no-Lipschitz class with its exact binary matching geometry. The resolved certificate result makes the rational panel optimum independently reproducible without elevating optimization infrastructure to the causal headline.
project_justification.fill: The project proves common sharp endpoint schedules and attained prospective causal-width identities for both response regimes, a rational budget-optimal panel formulation, simultaneous randomization-only outer coverage, and an exact deterministic certificate workflow. The workflow always terminates, passes every three-cell instance with at most five candidates by exact comparison with exhaustive enumeration and fixed-selection mixed-integer values, and collapses to a polynomial one-node certificate under a computable coordinatewise-minimizer condition; unrestricted trees may remain exponential.

prose_updates.related_work: Chen and Oberst (2025, Introduction, Section 4, Remark 3.1, and Appendix D.1) study reusable validation under bounded unit-level performance monotonicity and unit-level neutral-action equality, without a Lipschitz restriction, and prove tight bounds. The present conditional-mean monotonicity and neutral invariance are relaxations in aggregation, whereas finite \(\Gamma\)-Lipschitz smoothness is a refinement; the two unrestricted classes are incomparable. A homogenization bridge proves that the individual-level \(\Gamma\)-Lipschitz subclass and the aggregate class generate the same mean surfaces, and a separate no-Lipschitz theorem recovers the exact Chen--Oberst regime with binary exact-score or neutral matching costs. Anthony, Goyal, Gupta, and Nagarajan (2010, Section 2 and Theorem 2.2) supply the robust min--max \(k\)-median skeleton; the metric lift is informed by that result and does not claim its approximation theory. Cheung, Gleixner, and Steffy (2017) and Szeider (2026) motivate independently checkable rational proof logs; the present result specializes that goal to the causal action-score tensor by giving a deterministic finite branch generator, an exact bounded audit, and a computable condition for a one-node polynomial certificate. The NP-hardness boundary rules out any implied unrestricted polynomial-time guarantee unless \(\mathrm P=\mathrm{NP}\). The cited comparator papers do not supply this exact panel certificate result. Causal finite-sample randomization inference and adaptive policy evaluation remain distinct from the fixed-panel optimization question.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The common endpoint schedules establish simultaneous marginal lower and upper endpoints, not rectangularity of the full joint value set. The aggregate mean class and the no-Lipschitz individual-level class are not interchangeable: neither contains the other on nondegenerate populations. Exact score-distance gains require the finite-\(\Gamma\) subclass; monotonicity alone yields only binary exact-score or neutral-action protection. The exact certificate generator may enumerate every feasible panel and its branch tree may be exponential. The polynomial certificate conclusion is conditional on a feasible panel attaining every full-library coordinatewise residual minimum, and it is a statement about certificate size rather than an unrestricted polynomial-time algorithm. The outer confidence intervals are conservative rather than shortest, and scores, libraries, \(\Gamma\), and the budget are fixed before assignment.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The field contributions are the common causal endpoint schedules, the exact prospective widths derived from observationally indistinguishable fixed arrays, the faithful bridge to the individual-level Chen--Oberst class, and simultaneous assignment-only coverage. The finite-\(\Gamma\) identity is exact on the individual-level Lipschitz subclass and on the larger aggregate mean class because their induced mean surfaces coincide; it is not attributed to the published no-Lipschitz assumptions. For that actual no-Lipschitz class, the proved prospective cost is binary. The certificate question is resolved by a deterministic exact-rational finite generator and independent checker, an exhaustive three-cell, at-most-five-candidate audit, and a nontrivial sufficient condition for a one-node polynomial certificate. The project does not claim a polynomial-time exact generator on unrestricted instances, a polynomial certificate for every instance, a rectangular joint value set, optimal allocation, or estimation of future scores.

statement_notes.justification: This adapter records that the formerly open certificate handle is resolved by the already proved exact-rational generator and core-compression theorem, while preserving that theorem as the sole mathematical proof source.
statement_notes.gap: Generic exact optimization logs do not themselves establish a specialized generator, exact bounded audit, or polynomial-size condition for this causal action-score tensor; the underlying theorem supplies all three without an unrestricted polynomial-time claim.
statement_notes.consumer: Trial planners can archive a finite independently checkable proof of exact panel optimality, use exhaustive exact agreement as a small-instance audit, and recognize instances where the certificate collapses to one node.
